key_insight: LACUNA introduces a testbed to measure not just whether unlearning changes model outputs, but whether it truly localizes and removes memorized knowledge inside the model. It highlights a gap in current evaluation: output-level success may not mean internal knowledge has been erased.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of reliable benchmarks for evaluating whether LLM unlearning actually removes sensitive information from model parameters, rather than only hiding it at the surface level.
method: Proposes LACUNA, a testbed focused on localization precision for unlearning.
Evaluates localize-first, unlearn-second methods that target specific model parameters.
Measures whether unlearning mechanisms remove knowledge internally, not just at the output level.
impact: This gives researchers and practitioners a more trustworthy way to judge unlearning methods, especially for privacy-sensitive use cases involving PII. It can help prevent false confidence in methods that appear effective only because they mask outputs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing localize-first, unlearn-second workflow
Side-by-side comparison of output-level vs internal-knowledge evaluation
Model heatmap highlighting targeted parameters during unlearning
Benchmark scorecard for localization precision and residual knowledge
paper_title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
paper_authors: Matteo Boglioni, Thibault Rousset, Siva Reddy, Marius Mosbach, Verna Dankers
